prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics: general algebra, calculations with complex numbers, partial differential equations
Basic knowledge of physics: sensible and latent heat, heat transport mechanisms, ideal gas law
Basic knowledge of chemistry: atomic structure of materials

learning_outcomes.text: Explain why heat, air, and moisture transport are crucial for the hygrothermal design and analysis of building materials, components, and buildings.
Explain in his/her own words the storage and transport of heat, air, and moisture in building materials, components, and buildings.
Formulate heat, air, and moisture balances for hygrothermal applications, and apply the transport equations for heat, air, and moisture therein.
Classify building materials with regard to their hygrothermal properties, and evaluate the influence of these material properties on the performance of building materials, components, and buildings.
Design hygrothermically correct components and buildings, and analyze hygrothermically incorrect components and buildings.

syllabus_topics: Aspects of building sustainability, and health and comfort of building users

Theory of heat transport: 1) conservation of energy, sensible and latent, heat balances; 2) heat transport by advection, conduction, convection, radiation; 3) applications: U-value, equivalent temperature, thermal bridges; 4) non-stationary heat transport

Theory of moisture transport: 1) conservation of mass, moisture in air and porous materials; 2) moisture transport by diffusion, advection, and capillary transport; 3) applications: internal condensation, water absorption by and drying of materials

Theory of air transport: 1) conservation of mass, air in porous materials; 2) air transport through air-open walls and through openings; 3) driving forces for air transport: wind pressures and thermal stack effect; 4) applications: cavity ventilation, building ventilation; 5) coupled air, heat, and vapor transport
Concept and formulation of heat, air, moisture balances for building materials, components, and buildings
Building materials and their hygrothermal properties (load-bearing materials, insulation materials, air and/or vapor barriers, ...)
assessment_rules: The evaluation consists of two parts: an exercise test (40%) and a final exam (60%). Both parts must be retaken if the student fails. The procedure for retaking is similar to the first examination opportunity. Only a provided formula sheet and a self-brought calculator are allowed.
